pk.context: 0.5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: light beige, opaque soft gelatin capsule

tell: A 37-hour terminal half-life and 97% oral bioavailability set this 5-HT3 antagonist apart from its class.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 97%, and a high-fat meal does not change absorption. About 62% is bound to plasma proteins, and about half the dose is metabolized, with about 40% excreted unchanged in urine.
A hydrochloride salt that exists as a single isomer, with a molecular weight of 296.4 for the active moiety. It is a crystalline powder that is freely soluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 0.5 mg capsules, given as a single oral dose.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in known hypersensitivity to the drug; headache and constipation are the most common adverse reactions.
Prevention of acute nausea and vomiting from initial and repeat courses of moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy in adults.
Acts as an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT3 receptors, with strong binding and little or no affinity for other receptors. It blocks the vagal signal that starts the vomiting reflex.
The generic name begins with P and has twelve letters.
